newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity holds mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity holds mostly steady.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-West were mostly steady Wednesday with mild weather and little news to move the market, industry sources said.

Central Illinois Light Co said it expected to be back at full electrical generation capacity by Monday, Nov 11, after taking several units off line for maintenance, including the 366 megawatt (MW) Duck Creek coal-fired power plant which is expected to return to service Thursday.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) were talked steady for Thursday delivery at $18.00-21.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was assessed little changed at $12.50-14.00 for Thursday delivery.
Peak ECAR power for December was pegged relatively steady to slightly higher at $19.45-19.85 from $19.40-19.80 in Tuesday discussion, the sources said.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power for Thursday delivery was talked steady at $17.00-19.00 per MWh, the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power was said to have held steady at $9.00-10.00 per MWh.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), non-firm peak power for Thursday was talked steady at $19.00-21.00, the sources said.
Off-peak next day MAIN power was pegged steady at $12.00-14.00 per MWh.
Peak non-firm next-day power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) were talked at $18.00-20.50 for most of the region, down from prices of $21.50-21.80 in Tuesday discussion.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were reported to be steady at $12.00-14.00, the sources said.
Peak December SPP power was said to be talked higher at $22.60-22.90, the sources said.
